name: Santali (Ol Chiki script)

ancestors.notes: Santali macrolanguage/variety — Ol Chiki is the officially promoted native script for the same language already spelled in Latin as `sat`; see the `iu-Latn` precedent for a script-suffixed sibling spec.

notes: Ol Chiki (ᱚᱞ ᱪᱤᱠᱤ), the script invented by Pandit Raghunath Murmu (1925) and constitutionally recognised (2003) as Santali's own script (Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution), alongside the pre-existing Latin (`sat`) and Devanagari renderings. Unlike most Brahmic-descended scripts of the subcontinent it is NOT an abugida: it is a true segmental alphabet giving vowels letters of their own, so it is spelled here exactly like `sat` (Latin) rather than with the schwa/virama machinery used for Devanagari specs (`mag`, `new`, `gom`) in this dataset. GRAPHEME KEYS: 26 base letters map one-to-one to the `sat` Latin phoneme set (Zide 1972; Ghosh 2008); aspiration is spelled with the dedicated modifier letter ᱷ (`oh`) following the base stop, so the four digraphs ᱠᱷ ᱛᱷ ᱯᱷ ᱪᱷ earn their multigraph keys under design-constraint test 2 (an aspirated stop is one phonological segment, not two) -- the same test that licenses the Devanagari aspirate letters and Urdu پھ in AGENTS.md. `ᱦ` (ih) is polysemous /ʔ~h/ per the source grammars; `ᱶ` (ov) is the rare nasalised-w letter used in a handful of onomatopoeic/loan items. KNOWN GAPS: the glottalised-vowel and long-vowel distinctions that `sat` (Latin) marks with an apostrophe/macron are not yet written into the Ol Chiki base-letter set here (Ol Chiki marks length and glottalisation with combining diacritics ᱸ/ᱹ/ᱺ/ᱻ/ᱼ/ᱽ not yet catalogued from a primary source) -- left undone rather than guessed, per AGENTS.md rule 4 (no metric-chasing enumeration). No lexical/lexically-marked stress is described for Santali in the cited grammars (Zide 1972; Ghosh 2008): stress is left unencoded, an exemption rather than an omission. TIER: no WikiPron (or other registrable) gold set exists for the `sat`/Ol Chiki tag (checked against CUNY-CL/wikipron's scrape summary, 2026-08-03: zero rows under `sat`), so this spec stays at `skeleton` rather than claiming `research`.
